findings.defect: The pad cloud is much better placed than in round 2 (two banks left and right of the trench, vehicle and flame clear, apron lit warm) and the game's default view at T+1 to T+6 passes a first glance. On a second look it is cotton wool. (1) Lighting: in a8-liftoff-t6-side the sun is ahead of the camera (glint on the sea; the cumulus in the sky are grey with bright rims, median 124,123,122), yet the camera-facing sides of both banks are an even cream (median 152,144,135) with no shaded body, no bright rim and no visible shadow on the ground; in a8-liftoff-t10-far the cloud is a round, flat-lit grey-white ball (median 176,168,159, maximum 209) that sits on the pad like a sticker. In the lab by day the shading is a pattern of flat grey blotches on white (liftoff/t10-day). (2) Shape and motion: two near-symmetric sausage-shaped rolls along the trench axis with one scale of dimples (a popcorn pattern) instead of towers of billows; their outline hardly changes between T+1 and T+3 and at T+10 they are still a low layer that has not begun to rise. (3) The flame trench is empty: in a8-liftoff-t1 and t3 (3x crop at x 330-760, y 480-720) the open channel between the mount and its exit shows a clean floor and walls with an orange glow, the flame is a flat clipped white rectangle in the mount's side opening (x 620-655, y 580-605 in t1), and the cloud begins as soft fingers beyond the exit; nothing streams through or out of the trench.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/artemis2-launch-2.jpg (brilliant white steam shot sideways out of the trench, the brightest thing in the frame, with hard cauliflower detail); artemis2-launch-1.jpg and apollo4-liftoff.jpg (a lit side and a brown-grey shaded side, billows that tower over the pad structures within seconds); sts134-ssme-ignition.jpg (fire and steam boiling out of the trench itself); sts97-smoke-steam-night.jpg (strong side-to-side contrast).
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/smoke.ts: the sun term carries a large isotropic floor ((0.7 * lt.a + 0.45 * wide) * (0.5 + 0.5 * relief), added this round so that sunlit steam is 'as bright as a white surface with a floor of scattered light'), which drowns the shadow-march result lt.r, so the side away from the sun is as bright as the side towards it; relief comes from one noise band. The sources sit at the trench exits (padSmoke.trenchLength 78 in data/defs/visuals/plumes.json) and the 'away' term of smokeVelocity keeps the two flows collimated and low, with no emission inside the channel and little buoyant rise after the exits. The cloud's shadow on the terrain is weak or absent.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: vfx. Let self-shadowing decide the look: make the floor depend on optical depth towards the sun (bright where the sun side is thin, down to about a third of the lit value deep on the far side, blue-grey from the sky), keep the lit side near white. Add a second and third scale of billows that grow with distance from the exit and let the gas rise buoyantly (hot steam: several m/s after the first 50 m) so that the banks tower by T+6 to T+10. Fill the trench: a fast, bright, turbulent stream of flame and steam inside the channel from the deflector to the exit (emissive near the deflector, whitening outward), continuous with the banks. Give the cloud a ground shadow through the scene's shadow path. Re-shoot the a8 set from the side and from afar and compare the lit-to-shaded ratio of a bank with artemis2-launch-1.jpg (at least 2:1).

findings.defect: The cloud is on a different focal plane from everything else. Beside pin-sharp lattice towers, mount and hull its outline is a ramp 6 to 10 px wide at 720p and its interior holds no detail below about 20 px (Laplacian standard deviation 2.4 of 255 inside the sunlit cloud of liftoff-chase/t6-day). Small detached puffs still float over the apron in the game (a8-liftoff-t1 at x 500-530, y 485-510 and x 485-505, y 560-580; the hanging finger in a8-liftoff-t3 at x 470-510, y 560-640), and a dark worm-shaped hole opens in a8-liftoff-t10-far (x 700-725, y 650-667). Where the new outline sharpening acts on thin gas it makes hard-edged blobs with torn ink-blot holes instead of wisps (liftoff-probe/horizon-low.png, x 740-805, y 395-445, and the smooth tongue of the far jet beside it).
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/artemis2-launch-2.jpg and sts97-smoke-steam-night.jpg: steam and smoke are as sharp as the structures in front of them, with detail down to the pixel; thin gas fades as wisps.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/smoke.ts: the march runs at a quarter of the resolution in 30 steps and is rebuilt with cubic B-spline weights over 4 x 4 rays; the combine's outline steepening (edge = smoothstep(0.25, 0.6, sMax - sMin) about a noise threshold) moves the edge but adds no detail, so thin gas becomes a thresholded mask; 'hard' lumps gated by the gas's own density leave isolated cells that read as puffs.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: vfx, with the render core for the upsample. Add real detail at the silhouette: for pixels whose quarter-resolution opacity lies between 0.05 and 0.95 re-evaluate the last one or two march steps at full resolution with two more octaves of advected noise, or accumulate four jittered quarter-resolution frames (reprojected) to full resolution. Fade thin gas by density instead of thresholding it; drop cells whose connected density is below a small volume. Check in a8-liftoff-t6 that the 10-90 % width of the cloud's edge is at most 3 px and that the interior's Laplacian standard deviation is at least 5.

findings.defect: The booster flame is still a white stick. In the game it is a flat clipped white column (a8-liftoff-t6, x 628-652, y 560-700: 81 % of the pixels at 250 or more in every channel) with a thin orange rim, straight-sided, no wider than the hull and equally bright along the whole 290 px seen at T+10; no streaks along the flow, no shock diamonds, no ragged turbulent edge, no shimmer or smoke at its end, and the stage above it (85,74,68) shows no light from it. In the lab it is an airbrushed cream column with a soft orange edge of constant thickness and gentle sausage-link bulges every two to three diameters, ending in a brown translucent stain (liftoff/t10-day, y 330-440). In the engine tiles the sea-level flame is a white cut-out with a scalloped outline in tan haze and the detached island of flame is still there (engine-atlas-9m/sl-full.png about x 890-990, y 335; also sl-full-live), although the hand-off says there are no islands.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/liftoff-ascent/apollo4-liftoff.jpg and artemis2-launch-1.jpg (the flame leaves the nozzles streaked, widens steadily to more than the vehicle's width and breaks into fine turbulence, yellow-orange and then smoky); atlasv-oa6-liftoff.jpg and artemis1-launch-1.jpg (a wide glare that lights the air and the whole stack); sts51f-ignition.jpg (a hard, torn, brilliant edge). Methane-fuelled boosters on film: a translucent blue-violet to orange jet with clear shock diamonds in the first diameters.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/plumes.ts and plumeModel.ts with plume.methalox-booster in data/defs/visuals/plumes.json: the afterburn luminance still clips the whole cross-section along most of the length (the hand-off's own probe: eight times a sunlit white 30 m down), so the grading towards the tip and every internal structure are above the tone curve; the boundary has one low-frequency displacement (the bulges); the radius follows the nozzle cluster with no mixing-layer growth; the end of the flame is a noise threshold (the island).
findings.fixDirection: Owner: vfx. Clip only the first two to three diameters; let luminance fall by two to three stops along the flame so that its outer half is yellow-orange with visible eddies. Widen the jet with distance (mixing-layer half-angle of about 5 degrees) and replace the single wobble by edge turbulence at 0.2 and 0.6 of the local radius advected at jet speed, growing downstream. Show shock cells in the first diameters (they exist in the 10 km hydrolox tiles). End the flame by fading luminance, not by a threshold. Light the vehicle and the cloud from the flame as an area source. Verify in the game at T+6: under 40 % of the flame's pixels clipped and a width at 30 m down of at least 1.5 hull diameters.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/splash/impact-0.1s.png, impact-0.4s.png, impact-1s.png, impact-1.8s.png, impact-2.5s.png, impact-5s.png, close-0.4s.png, close-0.4s-live.png, close-1s.png; perf-chutes-and-splash.png
findings.defect: No longer a placeholder: the crown has sheets and fingers, is about one capsule height tall at +0.4 s, has broken up by +1 s and fallen by +1.8 s, and nothing hangs in the air at +5 s. It still reads as a stylised splash. The crown is opaque flat white (median 220,221,222 inside it; no translucent water body, no darker green or blue showing through, no sun glint, no shaded far wall), cut into pointed spikes like a paper crown or ice crystals, and it stands on a clean, hard elliptical foot. Blurred low-resolution mist puffs lie round the base until +1.8 s. The sea does not respond in any frame: no cavity, no collapse column, no ring waves, no reflection of the crown, and the capsule does not bob or settle. Every splash frame is taken on the vfx lab's flat Lambert plane: in three rounds no splash has been shot on the real ocean (hand-off 10.5), so the event as the player sees it could not be judged at all.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/heavy-seas-essex-1960.jpg (thrown water is ragged, translucent sheets with bright rims over darker water, lumps of very different sizes and a veil of fine spray carried downwind); apollo17-splashdown.jpg and dragon-crs1-splashdown.jpg (the sea round a capsule is dark, glossy, moving water). Orion and Dragon splashdown film: a lumpy wall of water and spray, its collapse into a boiling pale patch, and rings spreading two to three capsule diameters within two seconds while the capsule rocks.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/splash.ts SHEET_WGSL: the sheet is shaded as a white surface by the face the eye sees, with no thickness-dependent transmission or refraction of what lies behind it; rim, tears and ligaments are thresholds on noise, which gives pointed fingers and a hard foot where the sheet meets the plane. The water's own response is the ocean package's (request vfx-9, open).
findings.fixDirection: Owner: vfx for the crown, ocean for the water (vfx-9), the lead for a shot on the real ocean. Shade the sheet by thickness: thin parts transparent with a bright sunlit rim and sky reflection, thick parts white foam; break the rim into lumps and strings of very different sizes rather than spikes; hide the foot in a churning foam collar and a low ring of spray. Have the ocean displace: a cavity and rebound column at the entry point, two or three ring waves, foam in the ocean's own foam, buoyant motion of the capsule. Shoot the sequence at +0.1, 0.4, 1, 1.8 and 5 s in the integration lab or the game on the real ocean before the next critique.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/splash/close-0.4s.png, close-0.4s-live.png, close-1s.png (2.5x crops at x 380-900, y 270-550), impact-0.4s.png, impact-1s.png
findings.defect: Splash drops are still sprites: white rice-grain pills about 3 x 7 px, of nearly one size and one direction per region, laid over the crown, the capsule and the sky alike and not hidden or dimmed by the water wall in front of them (the hand-off concedes this). The crown's thin parts and rims break into a salt-and-pepper stipple of single pixels (close-0.4s at x 430-470, y 330-385 and x 820-856, y 338-400; close-1s at x 435-480, y 365-400) and a dotted lace hangs under the crown (close-1s, x 490-730, y 486-518). The crown's lower outline is one smooth hard ellipse.
findings.realReference: Splashdown film and out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/heavy-seas-essex-1960.jpg: spray is a continuum from sheets through ligaments to mist; single drops show only as glints or faint short streaks, and those behind a wall of water are hidden by it.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/particles.ts KIND_DROPLET: streaks with a minimum width, drawn after the sheet without a depth or transmittance test against it (spray sizes 4 to 50 mm collapse to the pixel minimum at this range). src/render/vfx/splash.ts SHEET_WGSL: the tears and ligaments are an alpha test on noise sampled per pixel with no filtering, so the transition is stippled; the foot is the sheet's cut with the sea plane.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: vfx. Draw sub-pixel drops with energy-conserving coverage (alpha = true area / pixel area) and a heavy-tailed size distribution; attenuate each drop by the sheet's opacity in front of it (write the sheet's depth and opacity before the particles). Replace the alpha test in the sheet by a smooth step one to two pixels wide in screen space (use the noise's screen-space derivative) so that rims are anti-aliased; perturb the foot with the foam collar.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/lunar-probe/hover-engine-on.png against hover-engine-off.png; out/screens/vfx/dev/i8-lunar-on-downsun.png against i8-lunar-off-downsun.png, i8-lunar-on-low.png, i8-lunar-on-upsun.png (integration lab, real lander and terrain); out/screens/vfx/lunar/30m-day.png, 30m-day-close.png, 10m-day.png, 5m-day-close.png, 30m-night.png, 3m-night.png; perf-lunar-descent-with-dust.png
findings.defect: The round-2 blocker is gone: the sky is black down to a sharp horizon in every lunar frame and the terrain is seen. What is left of the dust is too little and in the wrong place. At an 8 m hover the engine-on and engine-off frames are the same picture at a glance: a smooth pale patch about 240 px wide below the lander towards the camera (19 % brighter, local contrast down from 10.7 to 3.7) and a few faint radial streaks at the bottom edge of the frame; beside the feet the ground is 3 to 7 % brighter, to the left and on the far side of the lander it is unchanged (ratio 1.00 to 1.01), and the lander's long shadow at the left is neither softened nor crossed by streaks. Nothing reads as a sheet racing outward in all directions. Against the sun (i8-lunar-on-upsun) a fan of bright streaks appears only between the lander and the camera, like a starburst painted on the ground. At night at 3 m (lunar/3m-night) there is a soft white pool of light under the lander and no dust.
findings.realReference: Apollo 11-17 descent film from the LM window (sun behind the camera): from about 30 m bright streaks race radially along the surface, by 10 m craterlets and rocks all round the landing point are veiled by a thin fast sheet, and the sharp shadows of the LM and its probes fall on that sheet. Blue Ghost and Chang'e landing video: a ground-hugging ring of dust expanding in every direction with long streak shadows behind rocks. out/qa/ref/moon-surface/lm-falcon-lrv.jpg and mount-hadley.jpg for the black sky and the ground's tone.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/dust.ts after this round: a cap of one half on the veil, single scattering with albedo 0.36 x phase / 4 pi (so at back-scatter the sheet is no brighter than the ground it covers), a column that falls as 1 / r^1.5 from the scoured spot and a top at 4 degrees (dust.elevationDeg): only rays that graze the sheet close to the camera collect a visible column, and the phase function makes the up-sun foreground the only bright part. The streak pattern is tied to the ground rather than moving with the grains.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: vfx. Keep the bounded top and the black sky; put the dust back where it is seen. Raise the column within 3 to 10 nozzle heights of the foot of the jet and let it grow as the lander descends (little at 30 m, heavy below 10 m); add a back-scatter lobe so the sheet is 1.3 to 2 times the ground's luminance seen down-sun; make the veil act all round the landing point including the far side; move the streaks radially at grain speed (hundreds of m/s: motion-blurred lines, different every frame); let the lander's and rocks' shadows fall on the sheet. Extend tests/browser/vfx/lunar.spec.ts: at an 8 m hover the local contrast in a ring of 5 to 20 m round the feet falls by at least half on every side while the sky bound and the 50 % far-terrain bound stay.

Still clearly CGI: (1) in the integration lab by day, the view a player has, the plasma is a smooth pink-white fog lens wider than the shield that also veils the shoulder and the aft cone; the hull behind it is clean sunlit silver with windows and markings untouched, neither glowing nor lit pink; the wake is a barely visible haze shorter than the capsule; no streaks, no flicker, no sparks. findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/reentry-chutes/eft1-plasma-side-window.jpg (a dense field of fine, irregular streaks of very different brightness, pink-magenta to salmon with a white-yellow core); progress42-reentry.jpg and dragon-reentry-from-iss.jpg (compact clipped head, long thin trail). Hayabusa and Orion EFT-1 tracking film: the glow wraps the shoulder, the afterbody sits inside a luminous turbulent wake several body lengths long, sparks shed into it.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/plasma.ts: the layer is evaluated in the half-resolution volume and held one stop over white, so at chase distance by day it clips to a flat lens and its streak noise (six to one along the flow) is below what the march resolves; plume.plasma wakeGain 0.12 is too low against a sunlit Earth; nothing heats or lights the hull (the capsule's material is the vehicle package's; the plasma casts no light on it); the base flow behind the capsule is not filled.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: vfx, with the vehicle package for a heat-glow term on the capsule's shell. By day scale the layer and the wake with the scene's exposure so the stagnation region clips and the wake is at least as bright as the sunlit hull for three to five body lengths; draw the wake as converging, flickering filaments (two scales, advected at flow speed) and fill the base so there is no dark disc from behind; add a plasma light (pink-orange area source at the shield) on the aft cone and a temperature-driven emissive on the shoulder; emit fewer, larger, longer-lived ablation sparks. From the front show the shock as a bright rim with a darker, structured centre rather than a filled egg. Re-shoot dev/i8-reentry at peak heating.

findings.view: out/screens/vfx/splash/cut-away-1s.png (3x crop at x 420-840, y 100-300), cut-away-6s.png (3x crop at x 440-860, y 190-390), perf-chutes-and-splash.png
findings.defect: The released mains are no longer upright bulbs with their lines gathered below, but they are still not cloth. At +1 s: two ribbed bells with wavy hems, upright, pleats intact (jellyfish). At +6 s: each is a rigid, radially fluted rosette or gourd lying on its side, every gore still in place, with all its lines standing straight up from the hem to one point about 1.5 canopy diameters above it like a fountain or a birdcage; both are still in the air at horizon height and never reach the water in the sequence. Their shadows on the lab sea are black blobs.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/apollo9-floats.jpg (spent canopies lie flat on the water as limp bright sheets); dragon-crs1-splashdown.jpg (a canopy on the water, half sunk, its reflection smeared). Orion recovery film: a released main loses its shape within a second or two, streams sideways as a rag and settles on the sea beside the capsule with slack, tangled lines.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/chutes.ts (cut-away state, cutDrift in plumes.json) with canopyModel.ts: 'collapse to 8 % of the inflation' scales the same axisymmetric gore mesh, so it keeps its pleats and symmetry; keel-over is a rigid rotation; 'lines trail above the cloth' draws every line to one free point above the hem; sink at 9 m/s with no state for reaching the water.
findings.fixDirection: Owner: vfx. Break the symmetry on release: collapse gores by different amounts with large random folds, flatten the canopy into a streaming, twisting sheet aligned with the relative wind, and let it reach the sea within three to five seconds and spread flat there (floating, wetted, slowly sinking). Let the lines fall slack with gravity as loose curves of unequal length below and beside the cloth, not as a cone above it. Shoot +1, +3 and +6 s on the real ocean.
